headline: Will a coach ever see our small-town softball player?
dek: A composite story built from sourced paths. Kayla is not a real person. This is one ordinary path, not a formula, and it promises no result.

chapters.title: A starter nobody has heard of
chapters.what_was_happening: Kayla plays club softball and starts for a small-town high school. Few coaches know her program. Her parents wonder whether anyone will ever see her.
chapters.what_they_did: Her parents start with a plain question: what is realistic? They read the Eligibility: the 2 Hard Deadlines playbook so the paperwork is handled before the film.
chapters.how_it_helps: It takes one worry off the table. It does not make a coach call.
chapters.image_prompt: A fictional adult college-age softball player in plain gray practice gear sitting on a dugout bench at dawn, glove on her knee, empty field behind her. No logos or wordmarks. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9, no real school, NCAA, brand or league logos.

chapters.title: Is Division II a real option or a fallback?
chapters.what_was_happening: The family isn't sure Division II counts. In this composite, Kayla's club schedule puts her in front of coaches at tournaments, a pattern drawn from a sourced path.
chapters.what_they_did: They spend one evening on what each division offers, using the Camp ROI Playbook to decide which events are worth the travel money.
chapters.how_it_helps: It helps a family budget for exposure instead of paying for every event.
chapters.image_prompt: Fictional adult parents, a man and a woman in their forties, at a kitchen table with a laptop and a printed tournament schedule, coffee cups, evening light. No logos or wordmarks. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9.

chapters.title: Getting film ready for the coaches who are watching
chapters.what_was_happening: Coaches at tournaments see an at-bat or two. Kayla's family wants something they can send afterward.
chapters.what_they_did: They put together a short reel and a one-page profile using the Highlight Reel & Social Playbook, and check her public social accounts.
chapters.how_it_helps: A coach who finds you can see you quickly. It does not decide who gets a reply.
chapters.image_prompt: A fictional adult college-age softball player's gloved hand and a phone on a tripod filming a swing in a batting cage, warm indoor light. No logos or wordmarks. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9.

chapters.title: The one coach who keeps writing
chapters.what_was_happening: One assistant coach keeps emailing. In the sourced path this composite draws on, the player visited and committed where she felt at home. The rule that mattered: Division II calls, texts and emails are allowed at any time, and in-person contact and paid official visits open June 15 after sophomore year (D2 Bylaws 13.1.1.1, 13.3.1.2). The rule guarantees nothing.
chapters.what_they_did: Her family keeps a grid of every coach, date and next step with the Contact Log, and checks the rule at the source. The Contact Log is coming soon.
chapters.how_it_helps: A written record keeps replies from slipping. It does not create interest.
chapters.image_prompt: A printed contact grid on a clipboard beside a laptop showing an unreadable email inbox, fictional adult parent's hand holding a pen, soft window light. No logos or wordmarks. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9.

chapters.title: Visit questions that matter
chapters.what_was_happening: Kayla visits. The family wants to notice more than the facilities.
chapters.what_they_did: They go in with the Red Flags checklist so they know what to ask about money, playing time, academic fit and treatment. It is coming soon.
chapters.how_it_helps: It turns a good feeling into specific questions. It does not guarantee a good fit.
chapters.image_prompt: A fictional adult college-age softball player and two fictional adult parents walking across a quiet college campus lawn in autumn, seen from behind, no signage or logos. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9.

chapters.title: An ordinary ending, on purpose
chapters.what_was_happening: In this composite, Kayla signs with a Division II program where she feels at home and gets on the field as a sophomore. Partial aid, a normal college life, a degree.
chapters.what_they_did: Before signing, her parents read the Offers & Signing Day playbook on verbal versus written offers, and use it to compare in writing.
chapters.how_it_helps: It helps a family read an offer before signing. Nothing here proves a playbook caused a result.
chapters.image_prompt: A fictional adult college-age softball player signing a document at a table with two fictional adult parents beside her, pen in hand, window light, no readable text or logos. Cinematic editorial photo, 16:9.

closing: Kayla does not exist, and the ending is ordinary on purpose. Most college athletes play, study and graduate.
